inputs.text: The conflict between the US, Israel, and Iran is pushing global oil prices sharply higher and placing real strain on fuel costs in India. Even as the government reduces excise duties to hold petrol and diesel prices steady for now, this amounts to short-term meddling that drains national revenue and risks driving up inflation. India's heavy reliance on crude oil imports leaves us dangerously exposed to these foreign upheavals. We would be far better served by prioritizing energy self-reliance, national sovereignty, and the traditional values of prudence and responsibility instead of depending on unstable global forces that threaten our economic stability and the well-being of families.
